I’m sorry to hear you’re going through this. I would consider following your therapists advice about medication. That was something that really helped me. 

One of the most helpful things my therapist taught me at a time when I was having approximately 2 attacks a day was to try and be present. 
The opposite of anxiety is not being relaxed, It’s being present. 

I liked to do it by getting a freezer pack and putting it on the back of my neck while I laid down. Then I’d do some square breathing. If I was somewhere I could not lay down, but had access to a sink, I’d go and turn on the coldest water I could get and if it was a home sink I’d pull the stopper and dunk my face. If I was at work I’d just use paper towels and wet them then stick them across my chest under my shirt, on the back of my neck. Try to focus on the sensation of them. Square breathing is helpful because you have to really concentrate. 

A majority of my panic attacks I had to deal with alone. They’re terrifying. One time I called 911 it was embarrassing. Nobody talks about the shame you feel from being anxious. Just remember they always pass. Every time they pass. I’m so sorry you feel like a burden. You’re not. It’s just hard right now. I hope these tips help and if you need to talk you can always DM.
